subject: Staggered service ladder & regional failover add-on — pricing discussion
messages:
From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@stratiforme.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@stratiforme.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:17:00-08:00
Subject: Initial ask — tiered uptime + EU failover add-on

Thanks Rachel — quick summary of what Stratiforme needs as we scope renewal: we want a 99.95% baseline for the EU region, with a phased uplift to 99.98% tied to commit tiers across months 1, 4, and 9. Separately, we'd like a regional failover add-on (warm-standby in us-central) with an accelerated escalation SLA for incidents affecting query processing (>10% error rate).

Open questions for your team:
- Can you map commit tiers to list prices + step discounts (we're targeting 18% ARR uplift at scale)?
- Is warm-standby priced as a % of committed capacity or as a flat retainer?
- What does a 30-min vs 60-min escalation window mean operationally (who is on-call, when does the war room trigger)?

Attaching our internal reliability goals and a sample month-by-month traffic projection.

Thanks,
Sophie Turner
VP, Platform Engineering
Stratiforme Analytics
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@stratiforme.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — tiered uptime + EU failover add-on

Sophie — thanks for the clear summary and the projection file. Quick answers to start:
- We can support a staggered uptime ladder (99.95 -> 99.975 -> 99.98) tied to committed monthly throughput bands. I put a starter worksheet attached that maps three commit tiers to list price, and two discount curves (volume vs. term). See SLA_Pricing_Workbook.xlsx.
- Warm-standby is typically priced as a % of committed capacity (we recommend 35–50% depending on VM/GPU families) + a smaller retainer for prioritized failover coordination. We can model either the % or a fixed retainer if you prefer predictability.
- 30-min escalation means: SRE triage within 30 min, primary on-call engaged immediately, executive pager at the 2-hour mark for severity-1 incidents. 60-min escalation defers the executive pager to 4 hours and allows an extended triage window. We can provide a formal runbook excerpt.

I'll loop Vanessa for pricing pack options and Jordan for contractual language. Any preference on upfront commit term (12 vs 24 months)? That affects the discount curve.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Head of Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@stratiforme.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T08:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — tiered uptime + EU failover add-on

Hi Sophie — following up with concrete packaging options. I've sketched three packages in the workbook:

- Essentials (baseline): 99.95% EU, warm-standby priced at 40% of committed capacity, 60-min escalation, no retainer.
- Growth (recommended): staggered uplift path (99.95 -> 99.975 -> 99.98) with month 1/4/9 ramps, warm-standby at 35%, 30-min escalation, includes quarterly runbook drills and 8x5 SLA review. 10% volume discount at 12-month commit; 14% at 24-month.
- Premier: 99.99% available as add-on for a slice of traffic, warm-standby dedicated capacity (flat retainer + reduced %), 30-min escalation + named escalation manager, and annual tabletop + priority legal review.

A few negotiation levers we can flex: the % for warm-standby, whether the staged uplift requires explicit monthly gating (we typically use usage thresholds), and how credits are calculated for partial-hour outages. For the credits model, do you prefer a per-minute token or a slabbed credit by severity?

Attachment: SLA_Pricing_Workbook.xlsx — contains modeled price points and break-even math for each option.

-Vanessa
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@stratiforme.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@stratiforme.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T14:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — tiered uptime + EU failover add-on

Thanks team — we've reviewed the Growth package in the workbook. A few follow-ups:

1) We'd like the warm-standby priced at a fixed 9k EUR monthly retainer + 25% of committed capacity (this helps our finance team predict spend). Would Redwood accept fixed+percentage hybrid?
2) For escalation windows, we want the 30-min response but would like a guaranteed named escalation manager for the first 3 months post-commit (helps with onboarding). Is that possible without moving to Premier?
3) Credits: we prefer a per-minute token model tied to error-rate thresholds (min 15-minute granularity) rather than slab credits. Can you provide a draft credit formula we can review?

Attached: Stratiforme_traffic_adj.xlsx (monthly smoothing). We'll also upload the legal redlines by EOD; Rachel, Jordan — can you confirm who should own the redline review on your side?

Best,
Liam
Director, Cloud Operations
Stratiforme Analytics
